{"consolidated_memory":"**Loss divergence in ml/train/loop.py (two separate occasions)**

**OCCASION 1: [2026-01-22]**
- File: ml/train/loop.py (ml pipeline side)
- Problem: Loss divergence in training loop
- Trigger: Appeared only on first request after cold start
- Reproduction: Train two epochs on small split
- Signal: Loss curve turns upward and never returns
- Root cause: Off-by-one error in slice bound
- Fix: Corrected the bound and added a property test around it
- PR: #2945 on branch fix/loss-divergence-1
- Result: Nightly rollup matched source counts for 28 days running
- Note: Same corner of ml/train/loop.py as earlier loss divergence work, so context carried over

**OCCASION 2: [2026-08-10]**
- File: ml/train/loop.py (ml pipeline side)
- Problem: Loss divergence in training loop
- Trigger: Appeared only after client had already retried once (different trigger than Occasion 1)
- Reproduction: Train two epochs on small split
- Signal: Loss curve turns upward and never returns
- Root cause: Two writes that were never wrapped in a transaction (different root cause than Occasion 1)
- Fix: Wrapped both writes in one transaction
- PR: #6023 on branch fix/loss-divergence-3
- Stack: Python
- Covering check: tests/ml/test_train_loop.py
- Result: Cold start performance improved—dropped 20 percent, to 280 ms (different metric than Occasion 1)

These are two distinct incidents with different root causes, different fixes, and different outcomes, occurring 6+ months apart."}
